summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B universe expansion for the control-plane/security/compliance software node. The reference lane is anchored by Palo Alto Networks because its completed CyberArk acquisition directly maps to human, machine, and agentic identity security for AI-era workflows. The underfollowed lane emphasizes mid-cap or smaller public software vendors with more direct exposure to data security posture, exposure management, cloud/OT security, and Microsoft/SaaS governance rather than generic AI copilots. This is a research universe, not a trading recommendation. Layer 1B expansion found that the clearest scarce-control-plane chokepoint is identity and exposure management for AI-era cloud environments: human, machine, non-human, and agentic identities; cloud/AI exposure visibility; automated remediation; and regulated reporting/compliance workflows. The reference lane is Palo Alto Networks after closing CyberArk, which confirms that machine and agentic identity security has become a platform battleground. The underfollowed lane points to mid/small-cap software vendors where the market may be less focused on AI copilots and more on mandatory governance, auditability, exposure management, and remediation infrastructure. These are research candidates only, not recommendations. Layer 1B expansion found one reference anchor and three underfollowed public candidates tied to the AI-era control plane: identity/security platform consolidation, AI/cloud/OT exposure management, regulated compliance automation, and observability/security telemetry. The best underfollowed lane is not generic AI soft
